feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so I state no outcome for it. The best raced design is iteration 3 (score 893.56): the oval finishes 20/20 at 2.04 s, the s-bend 20/20 at 2.25 s, and the slalom 15/20, with all five slalom failures ending off track. Slalom steering_oscillation (0.25) and rms_error (0.012 m) are low, so the loop is stable and the remaining loss is off-track drift on the sharpest bends. The candidate is a single-variable change: base_speed 1.2 to 1.1, with geometry and gains (kp 2.25, kd 0.9, ki 0, sensor spread ±3 cm, sensor_size 0.016, mass 0.6, body_length 0.14) held at iteration 3 values. Iteration 1 and 2 showed the slalom losing the line at higher speeds, which supports trying a lower speed. The cost is small, since the oval and s-bend have time margin under 3 s. Read the race this way. If slalom finishes rise above 18/20 and the score beats 893.56, keep base_speed at 1.1. If slalom off-track events persist with base_speed at 1.1, speed is not the cause: the next change should be kd or the sensor spread, not a further speed cut. Check line_loss_events and max_error on the failing slalom runs to tell line loss from overshoot.
requested_changes: If slalom off-track failures persist at base_speed 1.1 (iteration 3 showed 5 of 20 failing at 1.2): leave speed as is and change controller.kd from 0.9 toward 1.1 or the sensor spread, since speed is then not the cause.

If the slalom and s-bend finish at 1.1 with completion_time well under 3 s: raise controller.base_speed in small steps (1.1 to 1.15) to recover time, since iteration 3 oval and s-bend finish times were 2.04 and 2.25 s.
If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 on any track at 1.1: lower controller.kd from 0.9 toward 0.7 with kp 2.25 held, since the iteration 3 slalom oscillation was 0.25.
